name: The Count's Likeness

source.note: A side quest boss of our own (The Count's Portraitist, docs/story/side_quests.md), built up from the guardian portrait: the great canvas the count gave his painter to copy from, an eye of the castle in a gilt frame, with a regard that frightens and burns the mind, a short list of the guardian's spells, and Legendary Resistance. Drawn with the guardian portrait's sprite, made Large.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (2/Day)
traits.summary: Twice a day, a failed saving throw becomes a success.
traits.text: When the Likeness fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead, twice a day.

traits.name: The Count's Eye
traits.summary: Whatever the painted woman looks at, the castle sees. The count speaks through it.
traits.text: The Likeness is an eye of Castle Ravenloft: what the woman in it looks at, the count sees, and he can speak through her mouth. Every portrait Tudor painted from it does the same, until it burns.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.summary: The Count's Regard or a spell, and a Frame Strike.
actions.text: The Likeness uses The Count's Regard or casts a spell, and makes one Frame Strike.

actions.name: Frame Strike
actions.summary: The heavy gilt frame swings like a door.
actions.text: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 10 ft. Hit: 16 (3d8 + 3) Bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: The Count's Regard
actions.summary: One creature within 60 ft meets his eyes; DC 16 Wis save, 5d10 Psychic and Frightened until the end of its next turn, half on a success.
actions.text: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 16, one creature the Likeness can see within 60 feet. Failure: 27 (5d10) Psychic damage, and the target has the Frightened condition until the end of the Likeness's next turn. Success: Half damage only.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.text: The Likeness casts one of the following spells, using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 16): once a day each, Hypnotic Pattern and Hold Person.

summary: A great canvas in a gilt frame: a young woman in a white gown, painted as no living painter could paint her, from a dead man's memory. It's an eye of the castle. Her look burns, her frame swings like a door, and the count speaks through her mouth.
